job: Driving a deny-by-default per-tenant authorization layer into the orchestration plane so flows authenticate and authorize before execution in a named release.
outcome: A named release ships per-tenant flow-/object-level authz as default-on, closing cross-tenant IDOR gaps without any opt-in flag.
motivation: Live-exploited CVSS 9.9 cross-tenant IDOR in Langflow proves the orchestration layer ships insecure-by-default and threatens enterprise trust.

task.who: the platform security and authorization engineering sub-team
task.what: Add deny-by-default per-tenant authorization checks before flow execution
task.where: in the agent-orchestration runtime's flow-resolution and execution path
task.when: from now through the Q2 2027 runway
task.why: to close cross-tenant IDOR gaps proven by live exploitation
task.how: owner-scoped authz middleware enforced on every flow resolution

job: Building default outbound-egress allowlisting with SSRF-hardened tool-call and web-request blocks so outbound requests are gated before leaving the runner.
outcome: A named release defaults to egress allowlisting with SSRF-resistant URL parsing, blocking internal-IP fetches from agent tool calls by default.
motivation: AutoGPT's CVSS 8.5 SSRF bypass shows arbitrary-URL fetch blocks are SSRF surfaces unless egress is locked down by construction.

task.who: the runner sandbox and networking engineering sub-team
task.what: Ship default-on egress allowlist and SSRF-safe URL validation
task.where: in the agent runner's tool-call and web-request execution layer
task.when: during the runway between mid-2026 and Q2 2027
task.why: to stop internal-IP SSRF via arbitrary-URL fetch primitives
task.how: allowlist gate plus canonical IPv6-aware IP filtering
